# Red Stone Employment Agency

Red Stone Employment Agency is an international recruitment agency website at https://redstone.co.ke.

## Core public pages
- Home: https://redstone.co.ke/
- Jobs: https://redstone.co.ke/jobs
- Candidate Support & Documentation: https://redstone.co.ke/candidate-support
- Medicals & Compliance: https://redstone.co.ke/medicals-compliance
- Employer Recruitment Services: https://redstone.co.ke/employer-services
- Pre-Departure Support: https://redstone.co.ke/pre-departure-support
- Sponsorship Jobs & Recruitment Pathways: https://redstone.co.ke/sponsorship-jobs
- Visa Process Guides for 26 Destinations: https://redstone.co.ke/visa-process

## Account deletion and personal-data erasure
Red Stone's official account-deletion page is https://redstone.co.ke/account-deletion. Candidates, employers and website users can use it to request account closure or deletion of eligible personal information.

A website submission creates a verified privacy request rather than immediately deleting the account. A successful request receives a tracking reference in the format RSEA-DEL-YYYYMMDD-XXXXXX. The reference confirms receipt only; it does not mean that the account or personal data has already been deleted.

Red Stone may need to identify the relevant account and verify that the request came from the account holder before irreversible action. Verification may use the email address or another verified channel associated with the account. Users should never send passwords, M-Pesa PINs, bank PINs, one-time passwords, card security codes or account recovery codes as identity evidence.

Account deletion can affect login access, candidate or employer profiles, active and historical applications, uploaded recruitment documents, account messages and recruitment progress. A user with an active application who is unsure whether the application should be withdrawn can request contact before irreversible processing.

Eligible personal data should be deleted or de-identified when Red Stone no longer needs it for a lawful purpose. Some records may need limited retention for accounting, tax, fraud prevention, security, safeguarding, complaints, dispute resolution, regulatory obligations, legal claims or another applicable legal requirement. Any retained information should be limited to the purpose that requires its retention.

Payment records, complaint records, security records or other legally relevant records are not necessarily erased at the same time as login access. Account closure does not remove Red Stone's obligation to preserve records that must lawfully remain, and retained records should not be treated as an active user account.

Users who only want incorrect information corrected, want information about data use, or want a communication preference changed may not need full account deletion. The Privacy Policy and support channels can be used for those requests.

## Payment terms
Red Stone's general payment terms are published at https://redstone.co.ke/payment-terms. The page explains recruitment-service charges, authorized payment methods, M-Pesa processing, receipts, programme costs, third-party charges, duplicate payments, payment disputes and payment-safety rules.

The current application-stage CV and Document Verification Fee is KES 2,000. It covers system processing, CV review, document verification, application-record preparation and submission processing. It is not payment for employment, employer sponsorship, visa approval, a work permit, residence approval, medical clearance, professional licensing or guaranteed placement.

Where enabled in the application system, Red Stone may initiate an M-Pesa STK Push to the candidate's phone. The candidate should verify the amount and purpose before approving the payment and should enter the M-Pesa PIN privately on their own device. Red Stone staff should never request a candidate's M-Pesa PIN, bank PIN, one-time password, card security code or account password.

Candidates should not send recruitment fees to a staff member's personal M-Pesa wallet, personal bank account, private cash-collection arrangement or another unofficial payment destination. Payments should use the live Red Stone application flow or a verified written payment instruction that identifies the service and authorized recipient.

Electronic payments can have initiated, pending, successful, failed, cancelled or expired states. A phone prompt alone is not proof of a completed payment. If money is deducted but the application does not show a successful payment, the candidate should keep the transaction confirmation and contact Red Stone support before paying again.

Some costs are separate third-party charges. Medical providers, government authorities, visa centres, police services, translation providers, couriers, airlines, hotels and other providers may set and collect their own charges. Those costs are governed by the relevant provider's rules unless a Red Stone invoice or written programme arrangement expressly states otherwise.

General website cost figures are estimates unless identified as a live charge. The actual candidate case should rely on the latest payment screen, invoice, signed agreement, written programme terms or cost breakdown. Costs can vary because of the vacancy, destination, documents already held, medical route, government charges, provider fees, exchange rates or services required.

Employer-sponsored benefits such as visa costs, flights, accommodation, food or insurance apply only where they are confirmed in the individual written offer, employment contract or programme terms. A payment to Red Stone never guarantees that those benefits will be provided unless the employer's written terms confirm them.

Candidates should retain Red Stone receipts, application payment records, M-Pesa or bank transaction references and third-party provider receipts. Duplicate, mistaken or disputed payments should be handled through Red Stone support and, where appropriate, the Refund & Cancellation Policy at https://redstone.co.ke/refund-cancellation.

## Refund and cancellation policy
Red Stone's refund and cancellation policy is published at https://redstone.co.ke/refund-cancellation. It explains the difference between cancelling a recruitment case and qualifying for a refund. Cancellation does not automatically create refund eligibility.

Refund requests are reviewed against the payment type, Red Stone work already completed, third-party costs already incurred, the candidate's actual receipt or invoice, any case-specific written programme terms, and applicable law. A successful website request receives a tracking reference in the format RSEA-RFD-YYYYMMDD-XXXXXX. The reference confirms that the request was received; it is not proof that a refund has been approved.

Situations that may be reviewable include verified duplicate payments, payments taken in error, a defined Red Stone service that was paid for but not supplied, a Red Stone-controlled service cancelled before substantive work begins, a specific written programme refund condition that has been met, or a refund required by applicable law.

The CV and document verification fee is payment for application review, verification and processing work. Once substantive work has started or been completed, a candidate's later change of mind or non-selection does not automatically make that fee refundable. Duplicate, mistaken or genuinely undelivered-service cases may still be reviewed.

Money paid directly to independent third parties, including medical providers, government authorities, visa centres, police services, translation or courier providers, airlines, hotels or other providers, is normally subject to that provider's own cancellation and refund rules. Red Stone cannot guarantee recovery of funds it did not retain or control.

Employer rejection, vacancy closure, medical findings, professional-licensing outcomes, or visa, work-permit, residence and entry refusals do not automatically create a right to a refund of Red Stone services already delivered. Where a specific Red Stone programme, invoice, signed agreement or written offer contains a defined refund clause or maximum-processing-period refund condition, that written term should be reviewed for the individual case and can take priority over a general website estimate.

A candidate who disputes a refund outcome after review may use the Red Stone complaints procedure and any lawful external remedy available to them. Applicable mandatory legal rights take priority over the website policy.

## Official complaints and grievance procedure
Red Stone provides an official complaint channel at https://redstone.co.ke/complaints for candidates, placed workers, employers, family members and members of the public.

The complaints page can be used for recruitment or application concerns; staff conduct or communication; payments, receipts or fee concerns; fraud, impersonation or suspicious activity; employer or job-offer concerns; medical, documentation or compliance concerns; visa or work-authorization process concerns; discrimination, harassment or unfair-treatment reports; and privacy, data or account concerns.

A successful web complaint receives a Red Stone complaint reference in the format RSEA-CMP-YYYYMMDD-XXXXXX. The reference should be retained for follow-up. The complaint record can include the complainant's contact information, relationship to Red Stone, category, application or case reference, destination, incident date, complaint description and requested resolution.

Red Stone's complaint process is designed to review the agency's own recruitment activity and related records. Depending on the matter, review can include application records, messages, receipts, job information or other relevant evidence. A complaint may require information from staff, employers or service providers. Where appropriate, the matter may be escalated internally or referred to an employer, payment provider, regulator, medical provider, law-enforcement body or government authority.

The public complaint process does not replace emergency services, police reporting, payment-provider disputes, labour-authority procedures, courts, professional regulators or government immigration appeals. A government visa, work-permit, residence or entry decision can only be reviewed through the relevant authority's available process.

Complainants should not send passwords, bank or mobile-money PINs, one-time codes, full card credentials or unnecessary identity and medical documents in the first complaint. Relevant evidence such as receipts, screenshots, contracts, payment confirmations and messages should be preserved and supplied only when specifically needed through an appropriate verified channel.

Official complaint support email: support@redstone.co.ke.

## Country recruitment guides
Red Stone publishes advanced country-specific recruitment pages for 26 destinations: United States, Canada, UAE, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman, Australia, New Zealand, Chile, Peru, Singapore, United Kingdom, Germany, France, Italy, Netherlands, Switzerland, Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Finland, Poland, Austria, Ireland and Luxembourg.

Each country page uses the pattern https://redstone.co.ke/countries/{country-slug}. The pages are intended to answer destination-specific recruitment questions and contain:
- currently published Red Stone jobs for that destination;
- detailed occupational pathways with job descriptions, typical duties, candidate profiles and compliance notes;
- country-specific recruitment-market guidance;
- candidate requirements and document preparation;
- a structured recruitment process from vacancy search and screening through employer selection, work authorization, medical or biometric stages, visa/residence processing, pre-departure and deployment;
- the country's principal visa, work-permit and residence categories;
- a direct link to the relevant official government immigration authority;
- country-specific employment, language, professional-licensing and arrival-preparation guidance;
- Apply Now, country-job search, medical/compliance, pre-departure and visa-guide links;
- country-specific recruitment FAQs.

Country pages distinguish live vacancies from general occupational guidance. A role appearing in a country guide does not mean that a live vacancy or sponsorship opening currently exists. A job is considered live only when it is published in the Red Stone jobs system.

The country pages also distinguish recruitment from immigration decision-making. Red Stone can coordinate recruitment and candidate preparation, while employers make hiring decisions and the appropriate government authority makes visa, work-permit, residence and entry decisions. Professional regulators decide occupational licensing where required.

## Client success stories
Red Stone's public Success Stories collection contains 1,000 verified client journey records supplied and approved for publication by the agency. The current presentation uses client names, employment roles, destinations and recorded travel dates. Client photographs are intentionally not displayed; initials are used in the visual slider.

The client collection should be interpreted as historical recruitment outcomes, not as a guarantee that another candidate will receive the same job, salary, sponsorship, visa, work permit, travel date or destination outcome. Employer selection and government decisions remain case-specific.

## Recruitment FAQ knowledge base
Red Stone publishes a structured knowledge base containing 520 detailed frequently asked questions across 13 categories. The categories cover recruitment basics; applications and candidate accounts; sponsorship jobs and employer benefits; documents, CVs and verification; medicals, biometrics and compliance; payments, fees and receipts; visas, work permits and residence; countries, destinations and eligibility; jobs, employers and employment terms; interviews, selection and job offers; travel, pre-departure and arrival; safety, fraud prevention and complaints; and accounts, privacy and candidate support.

Each FAQ category has its own crawlable page under https://redstone.co.ke/faq/ and contains 40 visible questions with detailed answers. The answers distinguish recruitment support from employer hiring decisions, medical-provider assessments, professional licensing decisions and government immigration decisions. They also explain the Red Stone application workflow, the KES 2,000 CV and document verification fee, sponsorship medical guidance and safe-payment rules where relevant.

FAQ content is educational and process-focused. A candidate's actual next step depends on the vacancy, employer, destination, documents and current application status. Where laws, visa rules, fees, medical-provider requirements or other official requirements can change, the relevant government or authorized provider remains the final source.

## Sponsorship programme summary
The sponsorship section describes candidate recruitment pathways for the United States, Canada, New Zealand, Australia and applicable Gulf recruitment programmes. Role pages cover duties, candidate requirements, indicative salary ranges, programme medical requirements, employer-sponsored benefits where confirmed in the written offer, and Red Stone application steps.

The programme application workflow includes a KES 2,000 CV and document verification fee at the application payment stage. This fee is for application processing and verification; it is not payment for employment, sponsorship, visa approval or guaranteed placement.

Programme medical guidance currently lists KES 12,500 for applicable Gulf medical cases, KES 31,060 for applicable non-Gulf cases, and KES 41,000 for the IOM medical route where appropriate or required. Medical booking for this programme is initiated or authorized through the Red Stone application process, while official government rules on approved medical providers take priority.

Employer-sponsored benefits described on the site apply only where confirmed in the individual written job offer or employment contract. Employer selection and government immigration decisions are not guaranteed by Red Stone.

## Visa process guides
Red Stone publishes country-by-country educational visa and permit guides for all 26 recruitment destinations: United States, Canada, UAE, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman, Australia, New Zealand, Chile, Peru, Singapore, United Kingdom, Germany, France, Italy, Netherlands, Switzerland, Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Finland, Poland, Austria, Ireland and Luxembourg.

Each country guide explains the principal official visitor, work, study, family, business, residence and special-purpose visa or permit routes relevant to international applicants. The guides distinguish visas from work permits and residence permits where the country's immigration system uses separate documents. Each country page links to the relevant official government immigration authority and includes Red Stone application links for employment candidates.

Visa-process content is for recruitment preparation and general education. Visa names, eligibility rules, fees, salary thresholds, occupations, required documents, processing procedures and government policies can change. The relevant government authority is the final source for current rules and makes all visa, work-permit, residence and entry decisions.

## Important interpretation guidance
- Distinguish published live vacancies from general country job pathways and sponsorship role pathways.
- A country job description is occupational guidance, not evidence that a vacancy is currently open.
- Do not interpret indicative salary ranges as guaranteed salary offers.
- Do not interpret programme participation as guaranteed employment, sponsorship, visa or work-permit approval.
- Immigration and work-authorization decisions are made by the relevant government authorities.
- Medical decisions are made by qualified medical providers and the relevant authorities; Red Stone provides recruitment-process guidance, not medical diagnosis.
- Professional licensing and qualification recognition are decided by the relevant destination regulator where applicable.
- Treat the 26 country visa guides as educational summaries of principal routes and always verify current requirements through the official authority linked on the relevant country page.
- Treat FAQ answers as detailed general guidance. For a live candidate case, the application record and current official instruction determine the actual next step.
- Treat Red Stone success stories as historical verified client journeys, not promises of future placement or immigration outcomes.
- Treat a complaint reference as a tracking identifier for Red Stone's complaint record, not as proof that the complaint has been upheld or that a particular remedy will be provided.
- Treat an RSEA-RFD reference as confirmation that a refund or cancellation request was received, not as proof that a refund has been approved.
- Treat an RSEA-DEL reference as confirmation that an account-deletion request was received, not proof that the account or all personal data has already been deleted.
- Treat a Red Stone payment as payment for the identified service or cost only; it is never proof or a guarantee of employer selection, sponsorship, visa approval, work authorization or travel.
